drafts.title: I ran 30 YC founder bios through an AI roaster — 27 got identical feedback. Here's the pattern.
drafts.text:
Spent a Sunday afternoon testing YC batch founder bios through an AI roaster (roast-my-bio). Expected variety. Got the same critique 27/30 times.

The AI called it "the credential stack" — Former [big company] → Built [thing] to [big number] → Now building [startup].

The 3 bios that escaped had one thing in common: they started with a specific observation or belief, not a credential.

Full breakdown with examples and a fix: https://tinytools-smoky.vercel.app/roast-my-bio/blog/i-tested-30-yc-founder-bios-ai-roaster-same-critique-2026/

Unpopular opinion: most founder bios are just job applications in disguise.

I tested 30 YC founder bios through an AI roaster. 27 out of 30 triggered the same critique — what the AI called "the credential stack." Former [employer]. Built [thing]. Now building [startup].

The AI's verdict: "You've optimized for being credible to a stranger in five seconds. You've accidentally made yourself forgettable to everyone who encounters you more than once."

The 3 bios that escaped? They started with something specific they observed or got wrong — not a logo.

drafts.title: I graded 100 real developer prompts across 22 quality signals. 73% scored D or lower. Here are the 5 mistakes on nearly every bad one.
drafts.text:
Built a prompt grader that scores prompts across 22 signals (role, context, constraints, format, examples, edge cases). Ran 100 prompts from devs of all experience levels through it.

Results:
- A: 4%
- B: 9%
- C: 14%
- D: 38%
- F: 35%

Seniority didn't matter. The same 5 mistakes showed up regardless of whether you've been coding for 2 years or 20.

Wrote up what those mistakes are and how to fix each one: https://tinytools-smoky.vercel.app/prompt-grade/blog/i-graded-100-ai-prompts-73-percent-got-d-or-lower-heres-why-2026/

Tool is free: https://tinytools-smoky.vercel.app/prompt-grade/

Unpopular opinion: most developers are really bad at writing AI prompts — and experience doesn't help.

I ran 100 real prompts through a 22-signal grader. 73% scored D or lower. The pattern was identical across juniors and seniors.

The issue isn't intelligence. It's mental model. We learned to give instructions to computers (precise, literal, complete). Language models need something different: role, context, format, constraints, and examples.

Leave out any two of those five and you're getting generic output you'll spend 10 minutes editing.

Article with all 5 mistakes + before/after examples in comments.
